entries.description: Register.

**Gitignore `project-verify-type.txt`**, with a comment naming the scope (machine × project) and the reason, in the same voice as the `local-overrides.yaml` and `copilot-catalog.lock` entries above it. Ship the falsifier **both ways** (`L-112-1`): one that plants the file at the repo root and asserts `git check-ignore` claims it, one that asserts a deliberately-tracked look-alike is **not** ignored — a rule that ignores everything is indistinguishable from one that ignores the right thing.

**Retire the `committed` vocabulary in `ai_router/verify_type.py`.** Rename the property to one that means "the project file answered", correct `to_dict()`, the branch-2 narration, the no-git-root error (*"nowhere to commit"*), and the setup message's final line so the bar reads *the file exists carrying the same value*. Do not change the resolution order or the repo-boundary walk.

**Resolve this repo, and prove it.** Run `verify_type --set COPILOT_CLI`, set `AI_ORCHESTRATION_VERIFY_TYPE` in the machine's user environment, and show `python -m ai_router.verify_type` exiting 0 on branch 1 with `copilot_preflight` still green. The canonical repo failing its own setup check is the symptom that opened this set; it closes here.
Targeted pytest; verify; close.
Registered Set 124 S1 (github-copilot/anthropic/claude-opus-5); plan seeded; no decision-review queue; start checklist posted.

Added anchored /project-verify-type.txt to .gitignore with scope rationale. Shipped 6 falsifiers in ai_router/tests/test_verify_type_is_gitignored.py (planted violations in a throwaway repo seeded from the REAL .gitignore, never the working tree). Mutation-proved both directions: unanchoring fails the nested look-alike guard; deleting the rule fails both fire tests; restored green.

Retired the committed vocabulary: VerifyTypeResolution.committed removed, resolved promoted to the real implementation, to_dict key committed->resolved. Corrected PROJECT_FILE_NAME comment, three docstrings, the guided-setup message (now names the gitignore rationale), the branch-2 narration and the no-git-root error. Updated the one production consumer (ai_router/__init__.py) plus three stale comments there. Added a structural falsifier pinning the retirement (no committed attr, no committed key, no commit wording in the setup message). Resolution order and repo-boundary walk untouched.

Wrote COPILOT_CLI (no DABBLER_* keys; copilot_preflight authenticates a live probe) and set AI_ORCHESTRATION_VERIFY_TYPE=COPILOT_CLI in the User environment. verify_type now exits 0 on branch 1 (was exit 3 at session start); load_config derives transport.profile=copilot-cli; preflight still green; git reports the file ignored and invisible to status. FOUND AND FIXED en route: write_project_verify_type embedded a header reading Committed on purpose: it is project configuration, not machine state -- the exact inverse of the ruling, shipped into every file the setup command writes. A case-sensitive grep missed the capitalised word, so it is now pinned by a falsifier asserting the written artifact.

Targeted pytest green: 42 verify-type/qualified-verdict + 62 transport/overrides/copilot-routing + 254 remaining load_config consumers. FOUND A LATENT SET 123 DEFECT: 10 tests in test_transport_profile_config.py and test_local_overrides_merge.py passed ONLY while this repo had no project-verify-type.txt. Their synthetic workspaces carry no .git marker, so find_project_root walked past the tmp tree to the cwd anchor and the real repo answered, deriving copilot-cli into configs declaring no transports.copilot-cli block. Proved by moving the file away (20 passed) and back (10 failed). Fixed at both shared helpers by bounding each fixture as its own project; swept the other six load_config consumers per L-069-1 and found the class contained.
Register.

**Retire `transport.profile` from `ai_router/local-overrides.yaml`.** Once the project file is gitignored, both files are machine × project scope and the seat-local override is pure duplication — the defect class `router-config.yaml:86` names. `config.py` must stop honouring it and name `python -m ai_router.verify_type --set <VALUE>` as the one way to say it.

**Choose refuse-vs-warn by the tiebreaks and journal it** (`decision_journal`). A hard refusal is louder but strands any seat mid-session on an expensive path; a warn-and-ignore is reversible and self-describing. Whichever is chosen, the message must name the exact replacement command — an existing seat (this machine included) carries the legacy key today and must not be left guessing.

**Replace, do not delete, the coverage that pinned the old precedence.** `test_project_file_beats_a_seat_local_override` asserts a precedence that stops being meaningful when the loser is retired; it becomes the legacy-key falsifier. Add the sibling that plants the legacy key and asserts the operator-facing message names the replacement.
Targeted pytest; verify; close.
Registered Set 124 S2 (github-copilot/anthropic/claude-opus-5).

Removed transport.profile from config._LOCAL_OVERRIDE_ALLOWED so no transport key is locally overridable. Once the project file is gitignored machine/project state, local-overrides.yaml occupied the identical scope -- the two-mechanisms-for-one-fact defect router-config.yaml names.

REFUSE, journaled to decisions.jsonl under prefer-reversible. Deciding case: a Copilot seat with no project file would, under warn-and-ignore, silently fall back to api and then fail validate_provider_api_keys on a seat that has no keys by design. Message names python -m ai_router.verify_type --set <VALUE> and DERIVES <VALUE> from the stale profile via VERIFY_TYPE_BY_PROFILE. Dogfooded on this machine, which carried the key: refusal fired naming COPILOT_CLI; after migration load_config still derives copilot-cli and copilot_preflight is green.

Replaced rather than deleted both tests that pinned the retired precedence: test_project_file_beats_a_seat_local_override -> test_a_retired_seat_local_transport_profile_is_refused, and test_local_transport_profile_overrides_shared -> test_local_transport_profile_is_refused_and_names_its_replacement. Added the replacement-command falsifier (asserts the DERIVED value for both profiles), a look-alike proving still-allowed overrides work, and a structural assertion that no transport.* key remains in _LOCAL_OVERRIDE_ALLOWED. Propagated the claim to router-config.yaml (two comment blocks) and verify_type.py docstring. MUTATION-TESTED: disabling the targeted message fails all 3 refusal tests; restored 44 pass. A first mutation attempt silently did not apply (CRLF/LF mismatch in the PowerShell replace) and a first version of one test passed under mutation because the generic Appendix B refusal also names the path -- both caught and fixed.

Targeted 194 passed. Full pytest run of record: 3991 passed, 9 skipped (618s). The first full run exposed 7 failures caused BY this session: TestPinnedOverrideRespectsIsEnabled (6) and TestSessionVerificationPathWasNeverAffected (1) call ai_router._init() with require_api_keys=True and had been passing on this keyless Copilot seat only because local-overrides.yaml set transport.profile=copilot-cli, which exempts the key check. S2 retired that override and S1 conftest guard already blocks the real project file inside the suite, so the config resolved api and demanded keys the seat never had. Fixed with the sanctioned placeholder_provider_keys fixture (Set 111 S2) at class level -- same machine-state-coupling class S1 found, surfaced from the other side.
